defense_analyst.prose: MIN's defense is built to attack the quarterback. It sends five or more rushers on 72.1% of dropbacks [dc1] over 308 plays [dc2], the highest rate in the league [dc3], and averages 4.9 rushers per dropback [dc4]. The pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) reaches 26.3% [dc5], also first in the league [dc6]. The payoff is a pass defense allowing -0.15 EPA per play [dc7] and explosive pass plays on 6.2% of attempts [dc8]. The risk is the deep shot, so SF should pair quick game and max-protection looks with occasional vertical shots against the blitz. Third down is a strength: MIN allows conversions on 31.4% of attempts [dc9] over 118 plays [dc10], third best in the league [dc11]. Against the run, MIN allows explosive gains on 11.1% of carries [dc12] over 226 plays [dc13] and -0.10 EPA per run [dc14], so SF's run game must stay on schedule rather than rely on chunk plays. On offense, SF posts a 56.1% pass success rate [dc15] over 296 dropbacks [dc16] and a 4.4% sack rate [dc17], with a pressure proxy of 11.8% [dc18] allowed. Its run success rate is 47.4% [dc19]. SF's protection has held up better than MIN's pressure rate suggests, so the staff should expect a steady stream of blitz looks and plan hot throws against them.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: The first matchup is MIN's early-down run against SF's run fits. MIN passes on only 49.9% of early downs [mc1] over 379 plays [mc2], and its designed runs go right 39.3% [mc3] and left 35.0% [mc4] over 206 runs [mc5]. Set the edge to the right and keep MIN on schedule. The second matchup is MIN's pressure against SF's protection. MIN brings extra rushers on 72.1% of dropbacks [mc7] over 308 plays [mc8], while SF allows 11.8% [mc10] over 296 dropbacks [mc11]. Use max protection on early downs and hot throws, and send a vertical shot only when the rushers come. The third matchup is third-and-long, where MIN dropbacks on 97.9% of plays [mc12] over 47 plays [mc13]. With Hockenson out, Jefferson should absorb volume at 26.6% of targets [mc14], so shadow Jefferson on passing downs. The fourth matchup is SF's third-down offense against a MIN defense allowing conversions on 31.4% [mc16] over 118 plays [mc17], and Jordan Addison's 92.3% snap share [mc18] over 3 games [mc19] means plan for both his presence and absence.
